description:
Split from 45e1b7e8 REQ-04 (aspirational): a recorded gate result names the commit the repository pointed at when the checker ran, but not whether the working tree matched that commit. A pass produced against a modified tree is therefore indistinguishable from a pass evidencing the commit itself. Recording the observed tree's cleanliness alongside the commit makes the distinction machine-readable.

## Background

45e1b7e8 landed commit-level build verification for merges (scripts/verify-commit-builds.sh) and left the general evidence gap to this issue: GateRunResult carries a commit field only. crates/jit/build_info.rs already demonstrates dirty-tree detection. Whether any consumer treats a dirty-tree pass differently (e.g. gate readiness at HEAD) is a behavior decision outside this issue: this issue makes the evidence readable, it does not change pass/fail semantics.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A recorded gate run captures whether the working tree matched the named commit at checker start (clean/dirty), stored in the run record.
- [hard] REQ-02: Machine-readable gate outputs (gate status, status-all, structured findings envelope) expose the tree-cleanliness field wherever the commit is exposed.
- [hard] REQ-03: Recorded schema/reference docs for the gate-run format state the field and its meaning; existing run records without the field remain readable.
- [hard] REQ-04: Tests cover a clean-tree run and a dirty-tree run asserting the recorded value.
- Out of scope: changing gate pass/fail or readiness semantics based on the field.
title: Record working-tree cleanliness in gate-run evidence
